headline: Researchers extended Yann LeCun's JEPA AI design so one model can predict physical, chemical and biological systems, and its top liver cancer suggestion killed more tumour cells in lab tests.
score_reason: Interesting range of results, but they are the authors' own, early-stage and mixed.
importance_line: Scientists hoping for one general-purpose model to guide experiments get a first broad test, but the evidence is the authors' own, the gains are uneven, and the cancer result is lab-stage only.
summary: The Decoder reports that a team led by PhAI Labs, with Stanford, Oxford and Princeton collaborators, built JEPA-Anything, which extends Yann LeCun's JEPA approach (models that predict an abstract summary of a system's next state) and, the authors say, beat a standard version on ten tests across physics, robotics and weather. Its top liver cancer idea, pairing the immune signal IL-18 with blocking the CD73 enzyme, killed more tumour cells in patient tissue samples and mice than either treatment alone, though the study does not show it could become a therapy.
